title: Hyvässä kunnossa
subtitle: In good condition — when adjectives take the case too

blocks.text: Every case ending so far has landed on a noun: autohuollossa, korjaamolta, autoni. But adjectives sitting next to those nouns have to agree — they take the same case ending too. This lesson shows you that matching rule, using patterns straight from the corpus.

blocks.translation: The car came in good condition.

blocks.title: Two words moving together
blocks.text: In English, only the noun changes shape depending on grammar; the adjective 'good' stays 'good' no matter what. In Finnish, hyvä matches whatever case its noun is wearing — hyvä, hyvässä, hyvän, hyvältä — like two dancers stepping in sync. Miss this, and a sentence like hyvässä kunnossa would sound as broken as English 'in gooding condition'.
Piece 1 — The core rule: same case, both words

blocks.content: Whatever ending the noun takes, the adjective describing it takes the identical ending. Hyvä kunto (good condition, plain form) → {hyvässä|grammar|inessive, agreeing adjective|good} {kunnossa|grammar|inessive|condition} (Lesson 7's -ssa, on both words). Kallis korjaamo (expensive repair shop) → tästä {kalliista|grammar|elative, agreeing adjective|expensive} {korjaamosta|grammar|elative|repair shop} (Lesson 7's -sta, on both words).

items.en: The car came in good condition.

items.fi: En osta osia {kalliista|grammar|elative, agreeing adjective|expensive} {korjaamosta|grammar|elative|repair shop}.
items.en: I don't buy parts from an expensive repair shop.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — Agreement with the accusative/partitive objects too

blocks.content: This same matching applies to the object cases from Lesson 26. Sain hyvää palvelua — hyvää (Lesson 1's hyvä, now in the partitive) matches palvelua exactly, ending for ending. Vaihdoin uuden osan — {uuden|grammar|accusative, agreeing adjective|new} matches {osan|grammar|accusative|the part}, both taking the -n shape.

blocks.title: Even genitive phrases follow the rule
blocks.text: Lesson 12's genitive works the same way: {ammattitaitoisen|grammar|genitive, agreeing adjective|skilled} korjaamon palvelu, 'the service of a skilled repair shop' — ammattitaitoinen matches korjaamon's genitive -n exactly. You now have enough case knowledge from Lessons 7-19 to build phrases like this yourself, one matching pair at a time.

items.fi: {Ammattitaitoisen|grammar|genitive, agreeing adjective|skilled} korjaamon palvelu oli erinomaista.
items.en: The service of a skilled repair shop was excellent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: What condition was the car in?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Auto tuli hyvässä kunnossa, ja sain hyvää palvelua koko käynnin ajan.
lines.en: The car came in good condition, and I got good service the whole visit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: And the price at the expensive repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Kallis, mutta ammattitaitoisen korjaamon palvelu on sen arvoista.
lines.en: Expensive, but a skilled repair shop's service is worth it.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: You don't need a new set of endings for this lesson — you need the habit of applying the endings you already know twice in a row. Find the noun's case, then simply stamp the identical ending onto its adjective. Once this becomes automatic, your Finnish sentences will suddenly sound far more fluent.

blocks.content: Hyvässä kunnossa: HY-väs-sä KUN-nos-sa (both words end in the same -ssä/-ssa sound — let that rhyme guide your ear). Kalliista korjaamosta: KAL-liis-ta KOR-yaa-mos-ta (both end in -sta — again, listen for the matching rhyme).

rows.en: in good condition (adjective + noun, both inessive)
from an expensive repair shop (both elative)
